problem: The sentence says spot welding 'makes one nugget per cycle'. Earlier the chapter fixed 'cycle' as one electrical cycle of 20 ms at 50 Hz, and a real spot weld takes several cycles of current. A student can read this as one nugget every 20 ms.
fix: Write: 'Spot welding uses fixed electrodes and makes one nugget per electrode stroke (one complete squeeze-weld-hold-off cycle), the current flowing for several supply cycles'.

problem: 'Electrode wear opens the contact face' is unclear. Wear makes the tip flatten and mushroom, so the contact area grows, not 'opens'.
fix: Write: 'Electrode wear flattens the tip, so the contact area grows, current density falls and the nugget slowly shrinks'.

problem: The list of four resistances is a grouped list, but it is written as if there is only one electrode contact and one sheet bulk. In the real circuit there are two electrode-to-sheet contacts and two sheet bulks, which is why textbooks often count seven resistance elements.
fix: Write: 'Grouped into four: the electrode bulk (two electrodes), the electrode-to-sheet contact (two of them), the sheet bulk (two sheets) and the single sheet-to-sheet contact at the faying surface'.

problem: The question asks for two reasons seam welding is not a different process, but the first reason given ('it uses roller electrodes') is a difference in equipment, not a reason the process is the same.
fix: Answer: (i) the heat is still I²Rt at the faying surface, with no arc, filler or flux; (ii) the rollers only place many overlapping spot nuggets next to each other, so the metallurgy and the four-step cycle are unchanged.
